key_insight: Bayesian inverse RANS can assimilate noisy 3D flow MRI data to infer both turbulence-model parameters and inlet conditions, producing a calibrated flow model with uncertainty estimates.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to improve turbulence-model predictions in biomedical and other confined turbulent flows when experimental velocity data are available.
method: Use Bayesian inference to formulate the RANS calibration as an inverse problem.
Assimilate noisy 3D flow MRI measurements from the FDA nozzle geometry.
Compare two differentiable algebraic closures: one based on mean shear rate magnitude and one on turbulence kinetic energy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the inferred models reconstruct the measured mean flow velocities without overfitting and also yield uncertainty estimates for the parameters.
watch_item: The approach depends on differentiable RANS closures and may be harder to apply directly to more complex or non-differentiable turbulence models.
paper_title: Data assimilation of flow MRI data into RANS models with algebraic closures
